knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Out parameter aliasing an input operand leads to incorrect results
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Operations with out= or in-place semantics may assume output storage is independent of input storage. When output aliases an input, hidden read/write ordering, accumulation, or kernel assumptions can be violated, causing silently incorrect values.

risk_dimensions.shape: Compatible shapes where the output buffer can alias an input operand, including bias-like or broadcast-compatible operands
risk_dimensions.dtype: Dtype combinations that select different kernels may have different aliasing behavior
risk_dimensions.memory: Output tensor shares storage with an input tensor, through same object, view, or storage offset
risk_dimensions.device: Backend-specific implementations such as CUDA may rely on non-aliased input/output buffers
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Operation invoked with out= or in-place mode where the output buffer is an input operand

failure_mechanism.description: The public API permits an out= buffer that aliases an input operand, but the underlying implementation may not isolate reads from writes, causing corrupted accumulation or incorrect output compared with a non-aliased reference.

input_exploration: Generate outputs that are the same object as each input operand
Generate outputs that are views or share storage with each input operand at different offsets
Vary shapes, contiguity, and dimensions to expose hidden aliasing assumptions
Compare behavior across CPU and accelerator backends
constraint_awareness: APIs with out= or in-place arguments often have undocumented non-aliasing assumptions
Aliasing may be more dangerous when an operand is both read and written in the same call
Backend kernel selection and memory layout can change aliasing behavior
oracle_strategy: Compute the same operation with an independent output buffer as a reference
Compare the aliased-output result against the reference result for exact or approximate equality
Monitor for sanitizer failures or memory corruption when output aliases input storage

transferability.reason: Any API that exposes out= or in-place behavior can violate similar output/input aliasing assumptions, especially when the operation reads and writes memory with backend-specific kernels or fused optimizations.

important_considerations: Explore aliasing between the output and every input operand, not only the most obvious one
Use views and shared storage with offsets rather than only identical object aliases
Compare against an independent-buffer reference to detect wrong results, not just crashes
Test across devices and dtype/kernel selections
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses for APIs with out= or in-place parameters that create aliased output buffers from input operands, run both aliased and non-aliased versions, and assert equality of results while varying shapes, layouts, dtypes, and devices.
